reply_text:
I’d hold the merge for these findings:

1. **[P1] Short bodies lose text and always get an ellipsis** — `src/excerpt.js:6–8`  
   There’s no check for text that already fits. `excerpt('hello world', 30)` returns `"hello…"`, dropping `world`; `excerpt('hello', 5)` returns `"hello…"`; an empty body becomes `"…"`. This violates the documented unchanged-if-it-fits behavior. Return early before finding a cut point.

2. **[P2] A word ending exactly at the limit gets dropped** — `src/words.js:2–4`  
   `excerpt('one two three', 7)` returns `"one…"` instead of `"one two…"`. The slice excludes the space at index 7, so the helper retreats to the previous space even though `one two` fits. Check the boundary at the limit too.

3. **[P2] Markdown stripping deletes literal characters** — `src/plain.js:3`  
   Removing every `_`, `*`, `~`, and backtick treats ordinary text as formatting. For example, `toPlain('Use snake_case and foo_bar')` returns `"Use snakecase and foobar"`. Strip actual Markdown delimiters while preserving literal characters.

**Integration gap:** `src/card.js:2` still only trims the body; neither new helper is called anywhere in the card path. If this merge is intended to enable card previews, that wiring is missing.

All **4 existing tests pass**, but they don’t cover these cases. Reviewed `59856d7` against `main` (`fb7eac6`); no files changed.
